steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Place the squash halves, cut-side up into a small baking dish, and bake until tender, about 45 minutes.

Bring the quinoa and water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the quinoa is tender, 20 to 25 minutes. When done, stir in the butter until melted, then season to taste with salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion, green pepper, and celery; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 10 minutes. Stir in the apple, and continue cooking until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes more. Add the garlic and ginger, cook 2 minutes more, then stir in the vinegar, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and red pepper flakes; season to taste with salt and pepper.

When the squash is tender, scoop out some of the flesh, leaving the halves 1/2 inch thick. Roughly chop the acorn squash, and combine with the quinoa and apple mixture. Spoon the mixture back into the squash shells, and sprinkle with the mozzarella cheese. Return to the oven, and bake until the cheese has melted and is bubbly, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Gingery Quinoa-Stuffed Acorn Squash
raw_recipe.description: This hearty dish combines quinoa with apples, veggies, and loads of ginger in an acorn squash bowl that is perfect fare for those blustery fall and winter evenings.

review.reviewBody:
I love this recipe! The flavors are wonderful and quinoa has a great lightness and fluffiness that acts as a fabulous base to present the gingery, spicy flavors of the mixture.

I have a friend who has a restricted gluten-free diet but always loved the flavors and coziness of stuffing so this has been popular with her, but also with the rest of the potluck crowd when I have made it.

I love how versatile the dish is too - you can substitute margarine for the butter and eliminate the cheese to make it a vegan dish; you can add nuts or a dried fruit (currants for example) to the stuffing; you can experiment with other kinds of cheese (I've used goat before and it worked well).

Deleted celery and added instead carrot and mushroom. Didn't use any sugar and added a bit of cumin and curry. Yummy! Also, easily filled 2 squash halved (4 pieces). Topped with curried toasted cashews.

filling enough for four to 6 halves (acorn squash are small). Too much quinoa (1/3 instead of 2/3 cup) and too much ginger. 1/8th the amount would still give it a touch of ginger without overpowering the other healthy ingreatients. Also it was dry. Add butter or oliver oil. We pass on this one.

I made this recipe just about as is, but I added sausage and omitted the sugar. I thought the sausage added a heartiness to make it a complete meal. Also, I used 3 acorn squash, filled to overflowing. Great recipe!
This was delicious. I added ground turkey to make it a main meal, served with cauliflower puree. Yummy!

I made this recipe for supper on a cold, windy November evening. I omitted the pepper flakes because they don't agree with my palate & used a Gala Apple that I had on hand. I doubled the bell pepper by adding a sweet red pepper and replaced the celery with finely shredded carrots. I also replaced the sugar with Stevia. The ginger, nutmeg, and cinnamon added a nice warmth to the nutty quinoa. I feared the vinegar would overpower the dish, but it did NOT. Everything came together really well. I roasted some of the squash seeds as a little crunchy topping. The hardest part was cutting through the squash! It's a filling, hearty meal for a chilly fall evening!

Interesting recipe! Read the other reviews and held back on the sugar and spices. Used stevia (1 tsp) and Chinese 5 spice with a little cinnamon. Use raisin soaked in wine since I didn't have any apples. Think apples would have been better. Need to use more cheese - I used combination of Parmesan and mozzarella. I liked the salty vs sweet play. Will make it again as it's a healthy and quite filling meal.

This is a great recipe, I cook my squash in the microwave and then get everything else ready. I would suggest reducing the amount of sugar a little bit, it can be slightly sweet. 

The mozarella cheese is a good complement to the flavors in the squash. Yumm!

On the advice of other comments, I used about half the ginger and I'm glad I did. I think it would have been overpowering with any more. I thought this dish was pretty good, but not great. I baked my acorn squash for 30 minutes and it was over-baked (mushy and brown). I'm sure this would have tasted better if the squash was not overbaked.

Just made this tonight. I gave it four stars because it's good but not spectacular. You can probably use half the amount of quinoa the recipe calls for. I had a lot of filling left over. I also used cheddar cheese since we didn't have any mozzarella. In the future I will mix some cheese in with the filling as well as sprinkling it on top.
Did not add any sugar and it was still fabulous!
I used red peppers in lieu of green just because that's what was in my fridge. I also omitted the apple. This was amazing!
It is dry and just tastes overwhelmingly like cinnamon.

It was just okay. This was a lot of work for what it turned out to be. There is too much quinoa and too much ginger. The ginger should have a better measurement in this recipe. I will not be making again.
I loved this recipe. Took a little time preparing but I just was in a zone chopping all the veggies. All the flavors complemented each other. I would definitely make it again.
We enjoyed this recipe! I added a 1/4 C of walnuts to mixture!
Will definitely make again. I substituted carrots for the celery. I agree with a couple other reviewers about cutting hack on the ginger. Other than that, I thought it was great.

I didn't measure anything out, except the quinoa, of which I only used 1/2 cup (precooked). This turned out absolutely delicious, and although it wasn't my first time eating quinoa, it was my first time eating acorn squash. And I can't wait to eat the leftovers tomorrow! :) By the way, I preroasted 4 squash halves, and with reducing the quinoa, the amount was perfect for the squash I had. Thanks for a great recip!
I did not care for the flavor of this dish!

This dish is wonderful. As the name implies it is full of ginger flavor. My boyfriend thought the ginger would be overpowering (whereas I LOVE ginger). Turns out he thought it was perfect and I think it might be a bit much. However, the ginger is a perfect match to the apples. 

This is a very inexpensive dish. Especially if you already have the quinoa on hand, as we did.

The quinoa comes out so fluffly. Yes, you have extra stuffing which we are going to serve as a breakfast side dish.
